title: Embedding contract versioning and client feature-gated dimensionality transition
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a deterministic, low-friction approach to change the canonical embedding vector dimensionality exposed by the platform without forcing immediate reindexing for all customers. This ticket designs a versioned embedding contract + server-side compatibility shims and an operational migration playbook so that: (1) clients can opt-in to the new dimension via a feature gate, (2) older clients continue to work with best-effort fallbacks, and (3) we can reindex at scale with controlled quality/latency impact.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- API responses include an explicit embedding schema_version and dimension field.
- Clients can request embeddings with Accept-Dim or schema_version headers and receive a 406-like guidance response when unsupported.
- Server provides two runtime compatibility modes: projection (fast, lossy) and proxy-reindex (async, lossless).
- Reindex jobs can be scheduled per-namespace with shard-aware throttles; we must be able to pause/resume without losing progress.
- Reranking endpoints accept mixed-dimension inputs for a limited bridge period (using projection or padding with documented quality degradation).
- Monitoring detects P95 latency regressions (>20%) or retrieval-quality deltas (e.g., MRR drop > 5%).

Design details:
1) Contract and metadata changes:
- Embedding payloads will add two top-level fields: "schema_version" (string, e.g., "v1","v2-512") and "dim" (integer). These are part of the stable API and must be returned for every embedding response.
- Service metadata endpoint (/v1/embeddings/meta) will list supported schema_versions and a recommended default. This allows clients to discover server capabilities.
- New client SDKs will expose request options: target_schema_version and fallback_mode ("project","reject").

2) Client feature gating handshake:
- New clients include header X-Embed-Accept: schema=v2-512. If the server cannot provide v2, it returns 409 with a "supported_schemas" list and a guidance URL.
- For servers in hybrid mode (supporting both dims), server returns embeddings in the requested version. If conversion required, server uses an optimized projection kernel (SIMD-accelerated) or quantized transform.

3) Compatibility shims and projection strategy:
- Projection is implemented as a lightweight matrix multiply (512->256 or vice versa) using precomputed orthonormal projection matrices generated from producer model token activations. We prefer orthonormal to reduce bias.
- When projection used on read path, we add an "approximation" flag in the embedding metadata to indicate lossy conversion.
- Padding/truncation is supported only as a last-resort fallback (zero-pad or drop tail dims) and must be disabled for rerank-sensitive routes.

4) Reranking path considerations:
- Rerankers require dimension parity. During bridge period we will support an inline projection stage in the reranker service with strict CPU budget limits. If projection exceeds budget, requests will be rejected with 503 and guidance to retry.
- Introduce a routing policy to prefer shards already reindexed to the new dimension for low-latency requests.

5) Reindex orchestration:
- Reindex jobs are namespaced and shard-aware. Each job will claim a set of shards, run a convert->validate->swap sequence, and emit a checkpoint per shard (checkpoint id).
- Jobs must be resumable by checkpoint. We store progress as a simple text token per shard in our job store (no nested JSON here).
- Backfill throughput controlled via tokens/sec and memory caps per worker. Default: 1000 docs/min/shard, adjustable.

Operational playbook (high level rollout steps):
A. Prototype: small internal dataset proof-of-concept for projection kernels and measure quality (P@10, MRR) vs baseline. (done)
B. API contract rollout: add schema_version and dim to responses; update meta endpoint. Clients tolerate this change. (in progress)
C. Introduce compatibility shim in pre-prod: enable projection mode for test namespaces; validate latencies and CPU.
D. Offer opt-in feature gate for customers in Console and SDKs; provide one-click reindex in Console UI.
E. Gradual reindex: start with low-traffic namespaces, monitor quality/latency dashboards. Ramp per metrics.
F. Cleanup: after 90 days of stable metrics, remove projection fallback for older clients and mark old schema deprecated.

Monitoring and alerting:
- Dashboards: embedding_latency_p50/p95, embedding_cpu_spend_per_request, reindex_progress_per_namespace, rerank_mrr_delta, rerank_latency_p95.
- Alerts: EmbedP95Increase (>=20% sustained 5m), ReindexFailureRate (>2% per shard), QualityRegression (MRR drop >5% for 1 hour).

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for projection kernels with randomized vectors and golden matrices.
- E2E test with mixed-dimension query/rerank pipeline using synthetic traffic.
- Holdout evaluation: compare retrieval quality against an offline holdout set before and after conversion.

Security & data considerations:
- Projection matrices are not customer data but treat generated matrices as internal artifacts; store in encrypted artifact store with access controls.
- Reindex jobs must inherit namespace ACLs; exports created for reindexing are ephemeral and deleted on completion.

Rollout impact and communication:
- Customer Impact: medium during bridge if projection used (documented accuracy tradeoffs). We will provide clear scoring of expected quality change per model pair.
- Communication: blog post + Console banner + changelog; pre-release emails to high-volume customers with recommended reindex windows.

Open decisions and tradeoffs:
- Whether to make projection matrices public (customers could precompute on their side) vs. closed proprietary transforms. (Action: confirm legal/OSS stance)
- Use learned linear transforms vs PCA/orthonormal basis — learned transforms likely give better retrieval preservation but need more compute to generate.
- How long to maintain legacy schema (suggest 90–180 days).
